newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX near record on back of derivatives.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX near record on back of derivatives.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index rose to within a whisker of the magic 3,800 point level late on Wednesday, with renewed record gains driven by derivatives and with few fundamental reasons for the advance.
The IBIS DAX index traded 56.96 points, or 1.53 percent, higher at 3,787.52 points in late trade, having earlier hit a new all-time high of 3,791.31 points.
The main factor behind the rise was volatility ahead of Friday's "triple-witching" of DAX options, DAX futures and stock options.
"This is a mostly options-led market, with everyone getting ready for tomorrow -- the index just drops or gains ten points for nothing," a Frankfurt trader said.
The trader said the volatility in the market, combined with a lack of fresh fundamental factors, was making trading rather difficult.
Forecasts from the Ifo economic research institute earlier in the day were well received by the market, a trader said.
"They showed that there are no signs of overheating and that there are still signs of growth," he said.
Among the star performers over the day was Volkswagen AG, which was up 25.55 marks at 1,244 marks in late trade, off a high of 1,263 marks earlier on.
"Volkswagen is a nice share to base an option on, because of the high price of the underlying," a trader said.

The group's annual general meeting did not reveal five month figures, as some had expected. The main news to emerge from the meeting was that the carmaker intended to keep up its programme of cost-cutting.
Also performing strongly was builder Hochtief AG.
Hochtief was up 4.70 marks at 83.10 marks, amid renewed interest in the construction sector, which has significantly outperformed the MDAX of medium-sized stocks in recent weeks.
Positive sentiment towards the sector did not extend to builder Philipp Holzmann AG, which was among the afternoon's big losers, down eight marks, 1.60 percent, at 491 marks.
Germany's banks had quite a rollercoaster ride because of the options expiry. Deutsche Bank AG was up 38 pfennigs at 99.22 marks, having earlier fallen to 98.22 marks.
Dresdner Bank AG was up 87 pfennigs at 61.97 marks, having hit a daily low of 60.60 marks.
